narrative:
On November 3, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 30.1%, with 866 cases heard out of 2,877 scheduled. This represents a decline in throughput compared to the previous trading day, November 2, where the hearing rate stood at 41.8%. The bias gap remains narrow, with commoners seeing a 31.2% hearing rate compared to 27.4% for government matters.

Performance across benches showed significant variance. Hall 31 (C.M. Poonacha) emerged as a high-performance bench, clearing 87.9% of its scheduled cases in its second session, while Hall 7 (B.M. Shyam Prasad) and Hall 8 (S. Sunil Dutt Yadav) reported no hearings in their respective primary listings. Other notable performance peaks included Hall 22 (Shivashankar Amarannavar), which maintained a clearance rate exceeding 59% across its sessions.

Hearing stage distribution reveals that preliminary hearings dominated the day’s productive output, achieving a 49.6% conversion rate. Conversely, orders (32.3% heard) and final hearings (23.9% heard) saw lower relative clearance, signaling a backlog in substantive decision-making stages. Admissions proved particularly difficult, with only 19.7% of the 737 scheduled cases being reached.

Case type distribution remained heavy on Writ Petitions (WP), which accounted for 1,324 scheduled entries but only a 31.4% clearance rate. Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) demonstrated the highest efficiency among major categories, with a 60.2% clearance rate. Other types such as Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) showed a sharp decline in output at 17.3%, significantly trailing the 50.9% clearance observed on November 2. The aggregate trend suggests a day characterized by lower volume throughput compared to the previous week's performance benchmarks.
